The benchmark in `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` is now a distributed-memory MPI Cholesky, and `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt` links MPI. No new files were added and the executable is still `cholesky`.\n\n**What changed**\n\n- **Distribution.** Rows are grouped in chunks of four and dealt out to ranks in a reflected cyclic order, so the triangular workload stays balanced at every step. Each rank generates only its own rows of the test matrix.\n- **Algorithm.** Right-looking blocked Cholesky with lookahead. The small diagonal block is factored redundantly on every rank, each rank solves its own panel rows, and the panel is exchanged while the trailing update of the previous step runs.\n- **Kernel.** The trailing update uses a register-blocked 4x12 fused multiply-add tile over a tile-packed panel, with column blocking so the panel slice stays in L2. Otherwise a nonblocking all-gather is used and polled during the update, so multi-node runs still overlap communication.\n- **Output and validation** are gathered to rank 0 and keep the same format and exit codes. At 256 ranks on hyperthreads it takes 254 ms, which is slower than 128 physical cores but no longer collapses.\n\n**Caveat.** The multi-node all-gather path was validated by forcing it on in a temporary build, not on an actual multi-node cluster.
